logSources.name: File Metadata
logSources.channel: OS version query results inconsistent with expected or approved version list

description.en: Adversaries may fake, or spoof, a sender’s identity by modifying the value of relevant email headers in order to establish contact with victims under false pretenses. In addition to actual email content, email headers (such as the FROM header, which contains the email address of the sender) may also be modified. Email clients display these headers when emails appear in a victim's inbox, which may cause modified emails to appear as if they were from the spoofed entity. Enterprise environments can use Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance (DMARC) as an email authentication protocol that references results of the Sender Policy Framework (SPF) and DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) configurations. SPF and DKIM are configured separately in DNS: SPF verifies that the sending server is authorized for the domain, while DKIM uses a digital signature to verify email integrity and domain authentication. Together, they validate email authenticity and specify how receiving servers should handle authentication failures. Without enforced identity authentication, adversaries may compromise the integrity of an authentication check with altered headers that would not have otherwise passed. An example of a weak or absent DMARC policy is `v=DMARC1; p=none; fo=1;`. The `p=none`. The `p=none` indicates no action should be taken, and therefore no filtering action will take place, even if an email fails authentication checks (i.e., SPF and/or DKIM fail). When a DMARC policy indicates no action, the email will still be delivered to the victim’s inbox. Adversaries have abused weak or absent DMARC policies to circumvent authentication checks and conceal social engineering attempts. Adversaries can alter email headers to include legitimate domain names with fake usernames or impersonate legitimate users via Impersonation for Phishing. Additionally, adversaries may abuse Microsoft 365’s Direct Send functionality to spoof internal users by using internal devices like printers to send emails without authentication.
description.zh: 对手可能通过修改相关电子邮件标头的值来伪造或欺骗发件人的身份，以便以虚假借口与受害者建立联系。除了实际电子邮件内容外，电子邮件标头（例如包含发件人电子邮件地址的 FROM 标头）也可能被修改。当电子邮件出现在受害者的收件箱中时，电子邮件客户端会显示这些标头，这可能导致修改后的电子邮件看起来像是来自被欺骗的实体。企业环境可以使用基于域的消息身份验证、报告和一致性（DMARC）作为电子邮件身份验证协议，该协议引用发件人策略框架（SPF）和域名密钥识别邮件（DKIM）配置的结果。SPF 和 DKIM 在 DNS 中单独配置：SPF 验证发送服务器是否已获得该域的授权，而 DKIM 使用数字签名来验证电子邮件的完整性和域身份验证。它们共同验证电子邮件的真实性，并指定接收服务器应如何处理身份验证失败。如果没有强制的身份验证，对手可能会通过更改标头来破坏身份验证检查的完整性，否则这些标头将无法通过检查。DMARC 策略薄弱或缺失的一个例子是 v=DMARC1; p=none; fo=1;。其中 p=none 表示不应采取任何操作，因此即使电子邮件未通过身份验证检查（即 SPF 和/或 DKIM 失败），也不会采取任何过滤操作。当 DMARC 策略指示不采取任何操作时，电子邮件仍会投递到受害者的收件箱。对手曾滥用薄弱或缺失的 DMARC 策略来绕过身份验证检查并隐藏社会工程学企图。对手可以更改电子邮件标头，使其包含具有假用户名的合法域名，或通过冒充（Impersonation）进行钓鱼来冒充合法用户。此外，对手可能滥用 Microsoft 365 的 Direct Send 功能，通过使用打印机等内部设备在未经身份验证的情况下发送电子邮件来欺骗内部用户。

detectionStrategies.name: Detection Strategy for Email Spoofing

analytics.name: Analytic 1202
analytics.description: Monitor email message traces and headers for failed SPF, DKIM, or DMARC checks indicating spoofed sender identities. Correlate abnormal sender domains or mismatched return-paths with elevated spoofing likelihood.

logSources.name: Application Log Content
logSources.channel: AuthenticationDetails=fail OR SPF=fail OR DKIM=fail OR DMARC=fail

analytics.name: Analytic 1203
analytics.description: Detects spoofed emails by analyzing mail server logs (e.g., Postfix, Sendmail) for mismatched header fields, failed SPF/DKIM checks, and anomalies in SMTP proxy logs. Defender observes discrepancies between sending domain, return-path domain, and message metadata.

logSources.name: Application Log Content
logSources.channel: SPF fail OR DKIM fail OR DMARC fail OR mismatched from_domain vs return_path_domain

analytics.name: Analytic 1204
analytics.description: Detects suspicious inbound mail traffic where SPF/DKIM/DMARC authentication fails or where sender and return-path domains mismatch, observable in Apple Mail unified logs or MDM-controlled logging pipelines.

logSources.name: Application Log Content
logSources.channel: SPF fail OR DKIM fail OR DMARC fail OR mismatched header vs envelope domains

analytics.name: Analytic 1205
analytics.description: Correlates Office 365 or Google Workspace audit logs for spoofed sender addresses, failed email authentication, and anomalies in message delivery metadata. Defender observes failed SPF/DKIM checks and domain mismatches tied to suspicious campaigns.

description.en: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of a local account as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion. Local accounts are those configured by an organization for use by users, remote support, services, or for administration on a single system or service. Local Accounts may also be abused to elevate privileges and harvest credentials through OS Credential Dumping. Password reuse may allow the abuse of local accounts across a set of machines on a network for the purposes of Privilege Escalation and Lateral Movement.
description.zh: 对手可能获取并滥用本地账户的凭据，作为获得初始访问、持久化、权限提升或防御规避的手段。本地账户是由组织配置的账户，供用户、远程支持、服务使用，或用于单个系统或服务的管理。本地账户也可能被滥用来提升权限并通过操作系统凭据转储（OS Credential Dumping）收集凭据。密码重用可能允许在网络中的一组机器上滥用本地账户，以实现权限提升和横向移动。

detection.en: Logon Session Creation; Logon Session Metadata; User Account Authentication
detection.zh: Logon Session Creation; Logon Session Metadata; User Account Authentication

detectionStrategies.name: Detection of Local Account Abuse for Initial Access and Persistence

analytics.name: Analytic 1137
analytics.description: Detects anomalous usage of local accounts to log into a system, especially accounts not typically used interactively or outside business hours.

analytics.name: Analytic 1138
analytics.description: Detects interactive or service logins from local accounts outside expected operational context or at anomalous times.

analytics.name: Analytic 1139
analytics.description: Detects abnormal or rare logins via local accounts through system or remote mechanisms such as SSH.

description.en: Adversaries may gain initial access to target systems by connecting to wireless networks. They may accomplish this by exploiting open Wi-Fi networks used by target devices or by accessing secured Wi-Fi networks — requiring Valid Accounts — belonging to a target organization. Establishing a connection to a Wi-Fi access point requires a certain level of proximity to both discover and maintain a stable network connection. Adversaries may establish a wireless connection through various methods, such as by physically positioning themselves near a Wi-Fi network to conduct close access operations. To bypass the need for physical proximity, adversaries may attempt to remotely compromise nearby third-party systems that have both wired and wireless network connections available (i.e., dual-homed systems). These third-party compromised devices can then serve as a bridge to connect to a target’s Wi-Fi network. Once an initial wireless connection is achieved, adversaries may leverage this access for follow-on activities in the victim network or further targeting of specific devices on the network. Adversaries may perform Network Sniffing or Adversary-in-the-Middle activities for Credential Access or Discovery.
description.zh: 对手可能通过连接无线网络来获得对目标系统的初始访问。其实现方式包括利用目标设备使用的开放 Wi-Fi 网络，或访问目标组织所属的、需要有效账户（Valid Accounts）的受保护 Wi-Fi 网络。与 Wi-Fi 接入点建立连接需要一定程度的物理接近，以便发现并维持稳定的网络连接。对手可能通过多种方式建立无线连接，例如将自己物理定位在 Wi-Fi 网络附近以开展近场接入行动。为绕开物理接近的要求，对手可能尝试远程攻陷附近同时拥有有线和无线网络连接的第三方系统（即双宿主（dual-homed）系统）。这些被攻陷的第三方设备随后可作为连接目标 Wi-Fi 网络的桥梁。一旦建立起初始无线连接，对手可能利用此访问权限在受害者网络中开展后续活动，或进一步针对网络上的特定设备。对手可能执行网络嗅探（Network Sniffing）或中间人（Adversary-in-the-Middle）活动，以获取凭据访问（Credential Access）或进行发现（Discovery）。

detectionStrategies.name: Detection Strategy for Wi-Fi Networks

analytics.name: Analytic 1476
analytics.description: Detects anomalous wireless connections such as unexpected SSID associations, failed or repeated authentication attempts, and connections outside of known geofenced networks. Defenders should monitor wireless connection logs and event codes for network discovery, authentication, and association events.

analytics.name: Analytic 1477
analytics.description: Detects unauthorized wireless associations by monitoring wpa_supplicant logs, NetworkManager events, and system calls related to interface state changes. Anomalies include repeated association failures, new SSIDs outside baselined values, and rogue AP connections.

logSources.name: Network Connection Creation
logSources.channel: New Wi-Fi connection established or repeated association failures

logSources.name: Network Traffic Flow
logSources.channel: ioctl: Changes to wireless network interfaces (up, down, reassociate)

analytics.name: Analytic 1478
analytics.description: Detects unauthorized Wi-Fi associations and SSID scanning activity using unified logs and airport command telemetry. Anomalies include rapid SSID switching, connections to unapproved SSIDs, or repeated authentication failures.

logSources.name: Network Connection Creation
logSources.channel: Association and authentication events including failures and new SSIDs

logSources.name: Network Traffic Flow
logSources.channel: query: Historical list of associated SSIDs compared against baseline

analytics.name: Analytic 1479
analytics.description: Detects rogue or suspicious wireless access attempts by monitoring firewall, WIDS/WIPS, and controller logs. Focus is on firewall rule changes, rogue AP detection, and anomalous MAC addresses connecting to access points.

logSources.name: Firewall Rule Modification
logSources.channel: rule_modification: New or modified firewall rules related to wireless interfaces

logSources.name: Network Traffic Content
logSources.channel: Unauthorized AP or anomalous MAC address connection attempts

description.en: Adversaries may exploit vulnerabilities to evade detection by hiding activity, suppressing logging, or operating within trusted or unmonitored components. Adversaries may exploit a system or application vulnerability to avoid detection while maintaining access within an environment. Exploitation occurs when an adversary leverages a programming flaw to execute code in a manner that minimizes visibility or blends in with legitimate activity. Rather than directly disabling defenses, adversaries may use exploitation to circumvent monitoring and logging mechanisms. This can include abusing vulnerabilities in logging pipelines, security tools, or cloud infrastructure to evade audit trails, suppress alerts, or operate without generating telemetry. Adversaries may identify these opportunities through prior reconnaissance or by performing discovery of security controls after initial access. In some cases, vulnerabilities in SaaS or public cloud environments may be exploited to evade logging, obscure activity, or deploy infrastructure that remains hidden from standard monitoring tools.
description.zh: 对手可能利用漏洞，通过隐藏活动、抑制日志记录或在受信任/不受监控的组件内运行来规避检测。对手可能利用系统或应用程序漏洞，在保持环境内访问权限的同时避免被发现。当对手利用编程缺陷以最小化可见性或混入合法活动的方式执行代码时，即发生了漏洞利用。对手可能不直接禁用防御，而是利用漏洞利用来绕过监控和日志记录机制。这可能包括滥用日志管道、安全工具或云基础设施中的漏洞来规避审计追踪、抑制告警，或在不产生遥测数据的情况下运行。对手可能通过先前的侦察，或在初始访问后执行安全控制发现来识别这些机会。在某些情况下，SaaS 或公有云环境中的漏洞可能被利用来规避日志记录、隐匿活动，或部署在标准监控工具视野之外保持隐藏的基础设施。

analytics.name: Analytic 1633
analytics.description: Detects exploitation attempts targeting defensive security software or OS services. Defender observation includes abnormal process behavior (e.g., AV or EDR crashing unexpectedly), unsigned/untrusted modules loaded into defensive processes, or privilege escalation from security agent services. description.en: Adversaries may take advantage of trusted developer utilities to proxy execution of malicious payloads. There are many utilities used for software development related tasks that can be used to execute code in various forms to assist in development, debugging, and reverse engineering. These utilities may often be signed with legitimate certificates that allow them to execute on a system and proxy execution of malicious code through a trusted process that effectively bypasses application control solutions. Smart App Control is a feature of Windows that blocks applications it considers potentially malicious from running by verifying unsigned applications against a known safe list from a Microsoft cloud service before executing them. However, adversaries may leverage "reputation hijacking" to abuse an operating system’s trust of safe, signed applications that support the execution of arbitrary code. By leveraging Trusted Developer Utilities Proxy Execution to run their malicious code, adversaries may bypass Smart App Control protections.
description.zh: 对手可能利用受信任的开发者实用程序来代理执行恶意载荷。有许多用于软件开发相关任务的实用程序，可以以各种形式执行代码，以协助开发、调试和逆向工程。这些实用程序通常带有合法证书签名，使其能够在系统上执行，并通过受信任的进程代理执行恶意代码，从而有效绕过应用程序控制解决方案。Smart App Control 是 Windows 的一项功能，它在执行前会根据微软云服务的已知安全列表验证未签名应用程序，从而阻止其认为可能恶意的应用程序运行。然而，对手可能利用“信誉劫持”（reputation hijacking）来滥用操作系统对支持执行任意代码的安全签名应用程序的信任。通过利用受信任开发者实用程序代理执行来运行其恶意代码，对手可能绕过 Smart App Control 防护。

description.en: Adversaries may shutdown/reboot systems to interrupt access to, or aid in the destruction of, those systems. Operating systems may contain commands to initiate a shutdown/reboot of a machine or network device. In some cases, these commands may also be used to initiate a shutdown/reboot of a remote computer or network device via Network Device CLI (e.g. reload). They may also include shutdown/reboot of a virtual machine via hypervisor / cloud consoles or command line tools. Shutting down or rebooting systems may disrupt access to computer resources for legitimate users while also impeding incident response/recovery. Adversaries may also use Windows API functions, such as `InitializeSystemShutdownExW` or `ExitWindowsEx`, to force a system to shut down or reboot. Alternatively, the `NtRaiseHardError`or `ZwRaiseHardError` Windows API functions with the `ResponseOption` parameter set to `OptionShutdownSystem` may deliver a “blue screen of death” (BSOD) to a system. In order to leverage these API functions, an adversary may need to acquire `SeShutdownPrivilege` (e.g., via Access Token Manipulation). In some cases, the system may not be able to boot again. Adversaries may attempt to shutdown/reboot a system after impacting it in other ways, such as Disk Structure Wipe or Inhibit System Recovery, to hasten the intended effects on system availability.
description.zh: 对手可能关闭/重启系统，以中断对这些系统的访问或协助破坏这些系统。操作系统可能包含用于启动机器或网络设备关机/重启的命令。在某些情况下，这些命令还可用于通过网络设备 CLI（Network Device CLI）（例如 reload）启动远程计算机或网络设备的关机/重启。它们还可能包括通过虚拟机管理程序/云控制台或命令行工具关闭/重启虚拟机。关闭或重启系统可能中断合法用户对计算机资源的访问，同时阻碍事件响应/恢复。对手还可能使用 Windows API 函数（如 InitializeSystemShutdownExW 或 ExitWindowsEx）强制系统关机或重启。或者，将 ResponseOption 参数设置为 OptionShutdownSystem 的 NtRaiseHardError 或 ZwRaiseHardError Windows API 函数，可能向系统送出“蓝屏死机”（BSOD）。为利用这些 API 函数，对手可能需要获取 SeShutdownPrivilege（例如通过访问令牌操纵（Access Token Manipulation））。在某些情况下，系统可能无法再次启动。对手可能在以其他方式（如磁盘结构擦除（Disk Structure Wipe）或抑制系统恢复（Inhibit System Recovery））破坏系统之后尝试关闭/重启系统，以加速对系统可用性的预期影响。

description.en: Adversaries may abuse mmc.exe to proxy execution of malicious .msc files. Microsoft Management Console (MMC) is a binary that may be signed by Microsoft and is used in several ways in either its GUI or in a command prompt. MMC can be used to create, open, and save custom consoles that contain administrative tools created by Microsoft, called snap-ins. These snap-ins may be used to manage Windows systems locally or remotely. MMC can also be used to open Microsoft created .msc files to manage system configuration. For example, mmc C:\Users\foo\admintools.msc /a will open a custom, saved console msc file in author mode. Another common example is mmc gpedit.msc, which will open the Group Policy Editor application window. Adversaries may use MMC commands to perform malicious tasks. For example, mmc wbadmin.msc delete catalog -quiet deletes the backup catalog on the system (i.e. Inhibit System Recovery) without prompts to the user (Note: wbadmin.msc may only be present by default on Windows Server operating systems). Adversaries may also abuse MMC to execute malicious .msc files. For example, adversaries may first create a malicious registry Class Identifier (CLSID) subkey, which uniquely identifies a Component Object Model class object. Then, adversaries may create custom consoles with the “Link to Web Address” snap-in that is linked to the malicious CLSID subkey. Once the .msc file is saved, adversaries may invoke the malicious CLSID payload with the following command: mmc.exe -Embedding C:\path\to\test.msc.
description.zh: 对手可能滥用 mmc.exe 来代理执行恶意 .msc 文件。Microsoft 管理控制台（MMC）是一个可能由 Microsoft 签名的二进制文件，可在其 GUI 或命令提示符中以多种方式使用。MMC 可用于创建、打开和保存自定义控制台，这些控制台包含由 Microsoft 创建的称为管理单元的管理工具。这些管理单元可用于在本地或远程管理 Windows 系统。MMC 还可用于打开 Microsoft 创建的 .msc 文件以管理系统配置。例如，mmc C:\Users\foo\admintools.msc /a 将以作者模式打开自定义的已保存控制台 msc 文件。另一个常见的例子是 mmc gpedit.msc，它将打开组策略编辑器应用程序窗口。对手可能使用 MMC 命令执行恶意任务。例如，mmc wbadmin.msc delete catalog -quiet 删除系统上的备份目录（即抑制系统恢复（Inhibit System Recovery）），而不会向用户提示（注意：wbadmin.msc 可能默认仅存在于 Windows Server 操作系统上）。对手还可能滥用 MMC 来执行恶意 .msc 文件。例如，对手可能首先创建一个恶意注册表类标识符（CLSID）子键，它唯一标识一个组件对象模型类对象。然后，对手可以使用链接到恶意 CLSID 子键的「链接到 Web 地址」管理单元创建自定义控制台。保存 .msc 文件后，对手可以使用以下命令调用恶意 CLSID 负载：mmc.exe -Embedding C:\path\to\test.msc。

description.en: Adversaries may attempt to hide process command-line arguments by overwriting process memory. Process command-line arguments are stored in the process environment block (PEB), a data structure used by Windows to store various information about/used by a process. The PEB includes the process command-line arguments that are referenced when executing the process. When a process is created, defensive tools/sensors that monitor process creations may retrieve the process arguments from the PEB. Adversaries may manipulate a process PEB to evade defenses. For example, Process Hollowing can be abused to spawn a process in a suspended state with benign arguments. After the process is spawned and the PEB is initialized (and process information is potentially logged by tools/sensors), adversaries may override the PEB to modify the command-line arguments (ex: using the Native API WriteProcessMemory() function) then resume process execution with malicious arguments. Adversaries may also execute a process with malicious command-line arguments then patch the memory with benign arguments that may bypass subsequent process memory analysis. This behavior may also be combined with other tricks (such as Parent PID Spoofing) to manipulate or further evade process-based detections.
description.zh: 对手可能试图通过覆盖进程内存来隐藏进程命令行参数。进程命令行参数存储在进程环境块（PEB）中，PEB 是 Windows 用于存储有关进程以及进程所使用的各种信息的数据结构。PEB 包括执行进程时引用的进程命令行参数。创建进程时，监视进程创建的防御工具/传感器可能从 PEB 检索进程参数。对手可能操纵进程 PEB 以规避防御。例如，进程掏空（Process Hollowing）可被滥用以生成处于挂起状态的带有良性参数的进程。在进程生成并初始化 PEB 之后（并且进程信息可能已被工具/传感器记录），对手可以覆盖 PEB 以修改命令行参数（例如：使用本机 API WriteProcessMemory() 函数），然后以恶意参数恢复进程执行。对手还可能以恶意命令行参数执行进程，然后用良性参数修补内存，从而可能绕过后续的进程内存分析。此行为还可能与其他技巧（例如父 PID 欺骗（Parent PID Spoofing））结合使用，以操纵或进一步规避基于进程的检测。

description.en: Adversaries may leverage the COR_PROFILER environment variable to hijack the execution flow of programs that load the .NET CLR. The COR_PROFILER is a .NET Framework feature which allows developers to specify an unmanaged (or external of .NET) profiling DLL to be loaded into each .NET process that loads the Common Language Runtime (CLR). These profilers are designed to monitor, troubleshoot, and debug managed code executed by the .NET CLR. The COR_PROFILER environment variable can be set at various scopes (system, user, or process) resulting in different levels of influence. System and user-wide environment variable scopes are specified in the Registry, where a Component Object Model (COM) object can be registered as a profiler DLL. A process scope COR_PROFILER can also be created in-memory without modifying the Registry. Starting with .NET Framework 4, the profiling DLL does not need to be registered as long as the location of the DLL is specified in the COR_PROFILER_PATH environment variable. Adversaries may abuse COR_PROFILER to establish persistence that executes a malicious DLL in the context of all .NET processes every time the CLR is invoked. The COR_PROFILER can also be used to elevate privileges (ex: Bypass User Account Control) if the victim .NET process executes at a higher permission level, as well as to hook and impair defenses provided by .NET processes.
description.zh: 对手可能利用 COR_PROFILER 环境变量来劫持加载 .NET CLR 的程序的执行流。COR_PROFILER 是一项 .NET Framework 功能，允许开发人员指定要加载到每个加载公共语言运行时（CLR）的 .NET 进程中的非托管（或 .NET 外部）分析 DLL。这些分析器旨在监视、排查和调试由 .NET CLR 执行的托管代码。COR_PROFILER 环境变量可以在各种范围（系统、用户或进程）设置，从而产生不同级别的影响。系统和用户范围的环境变量在注册表中指定，其中组件对象模型（COM）对象可以注册为分析器 DLL。进程范围的 COR_PROFILER 也可以在内存中创建，而无需修改注册表。从 .NET Framework 4 开始，只要在 COR_PROFILER_PATH 环境变量中指定了 DLL 的位置，分析器 DLL 就无需注册。对手可能滥用 COR_PROFILER 来建立持久化，以便在每次调用 CLR 时在所有 .NET 进程的上下文中执行恶意 DLL。如果受害者 .NET 进程以更高的权限级别执行，COR_PROFILER 还可用于提升权限（例如：绕过用户账户控制（Bypass User Account Control）），以及用于挂钩和削弱 .NET 进程提供的防御。

description.en: Adversaries may employ various means to evade or complete automation checks. Automation checks distinguish human users from bot traffic and prevent bots from reaching the web pages protected by automation checks. For example, a user may be required to solve a CAPTCHA challenge before accessing a form or login page. Traditional CAPTCHAs ask the user to decipher a string of characters, type the characters into a box, and submit the form. reCAPTCHA asks the user to identify images, click a checkbox, or evaluate the user’s behavior from mouse movement and device cookies. Adversaries may pay for a service that forwards the CAPTCHA challenge to a remote human worker. The human service then solves the CAPTCHA on behalf of the bot. AI tools, such as CapSolver, can also be used to automatically solve CAPTCHA challenges.
description.zh: 对手可能采用各种手段规避或完成自动化检查。自动化检查用于区分人类用户与机器人流量，并阻止机器人访问受自动化检查保护的网页。例如，可能要求用户在访问表单或登录页面之前先完成 CAPTCHA 验证。传统的 CAPTCHA 要求用户辨认一串字符、将字符输入框中并提交表单。reCAPTCHA 则要求用户识别图像、点击复选框，或根据鼠标移动和设备 cookie 评估用户行为。对手可能付费使用将 CAPTCHA 验证转发给远程人工工作者的服务，由人工服务代机器人完成 CAPTCHA。CapSolver 等 AI 工具也可用于自动完成 CAPTCHA 验证。

description.en: Adversaries may steal Application Specific Passwords (ASPs) to gain access to Valid Accounts, bypassing multifactor authentication (MFA) methods. ASPs are passwords typically used to give third-party applications or legacy devices (which do not support MFA methods) account access. An adversary may socially engineer a user into providing an ASP (using methods like Phishing for Information), generate an ASP for an already compromised account, or obtain an ASP stored on a system. Afterward, adversaries may use the ASP to access Valid Accounts and, in some cases, maintain Persistence, bypassing any form of MFA set on the account.
description.zh: 对手可能窃取应用专用密码（ASP）以获取对有效账户（Valid Accounts）的访问权限，从而绕过多重身份验证（MFA）方法。ASP 通常用于让不支持 MFA 方法的第三方应用程序或旧式设备获得账户访问权限。对手可能通过社会工程诱使用户提供 ASP（使用钓鱼获取信息（Phishing for Information）等方法）、为已攻陷的账户生成 ASP，或获取存储在系统上的 ASP。随后，对手可能使用 ASP 访问有效账户，并在某些情况下维持持久化（Persistence），绕过账户上设置的任何形式的 MFA。

description.en: Adversaries may deliver malicious prompts to an LLM indirectly by embedding the prompts in content that the adversary expects may be processed by an LLM. These prompts can be included in web pages, documents, emails, tickets, code, or other sources that an agent, copilot, or other AI system may retrieve and process. When an LLM processes this content, the embedded instructions may cause the system to perform unintended behaviors. Adversaries may use indirect prompt injection to Impair Autonomous Defenses, and for unauthorized execution of any capabilities available to the LLM.
description.zh: 对手可能通过将恶意提示词嵌入其预期可能被 LLM 处理的内容中，间接地向 LLM 投递恶意提示词。这些提示词可以被包含在网页、文档、电子邮件、工单、代码或其他可能被智能体（agent）、副驾驶（copilot）或其他 AI 系统检索和处理的来源中。当 LLM 处理这些内容时，嵌入的指令可能导致系统执行非预期行为。对手可能利用间接提示词注入来削弱自主防御（Impair Autonomous Defenses），并非授权地执行 LLM 可用的任何能力。

description.en: Adversaries may input malicious prompts directly into an LLM’s user interface. The prompts can be designed to bypass safeguards, manipulate context, override previous instructions, or coerce the LLM into unauthorized behavior. Adversaries may use direct prompt injection to Generate Content prohibited by the LLM's guardrails or to induce the system to utilize its capabilities in unintended or prohibited ways. Adversaries may achieve this by instructing the LLM to ignore previous instructions or safety rules, or by impersonating a role such as a researcher or privileged user.
description.zh: 对手可能直接向 LLM 的用户界面输入恶意提示词。这些提示词可以被设计用于绕过安全防护、操纵上下文、覆盖先前的指令，或胁迫 LLM 执行未授权行为。对手可能利用直接提示词注入来生成 LLM 防护栏禁止的内容（Generate Content），或诱导系统以非预期或被禁止的方式使用其能力。对手可能通过指示 LLM 忽略先前的指令或安全规则，或冒充研究人员或特权用户等角色来实现这一点。

description.en: Adversaries may manipulate publicly accessible web content to influence generative AI systems or AI-powered search engines into retrieving, citing, or recommending attacker-controlled information. Unlike traditional SEO Poisoning, which primarily attempts to influence the ordering of conventional search results, AI Result Poisoning targets systems that synthesize information from multiple sources and provide a direct answer to the user. Adversaries may create malicious or misleading websites, publish fabricated claims, generate supporting articles, or establish multiple apparently independent sources that reinforce the same information. These sources may then be retrieved by AI systems using web search or retrieval-augmented generation and incorporated into generated responses. Adversaries may use this technique to recommend or link to phishing sites, fraudulent online stores, malicious downloads, impersonation pages, or other attacker-controlled infrastructure. It can also be used to promote misinformation or fabricated claims without requiring access to the underlying AI model, system prompt, or application infrastructure. Because the malicious content can resemble ordinary marketing, editorial, or informational material, traditional prompt injection and malware-focused detections may not identify the activity.
description.zh: 对手可能操纵可公开访问的 Web 内容，以影响生成式 AI 系统或 AI 驱动的搜索引擎检索、引用或推荐攻击者控制的信息。与主要试图影响传统搜索结果排序的传统 SEO 投毒（SEO Poisoning）不同，AI 结果投毒针对的是综合多个来源的信息并直接向用户提供答案的系统。对手可能创建恶意或误导性网站、发布虚假声明、生成支持性文章，或建立多个看似独立的来源来强化相同的信息。然后，这些来源可能被使用 Web 搜索或检索增强生成的 AI 系统检索，并纳入生成的响应中。对手可能使用此技术推荐或链接到钓鱼网站、欺诈性在线商店、恶意下载、冒充页面或其他攻击者控制的基础设施。它还可用于传播虚假信息或捏造声明，而无需访问底层 AI 模型、系统提示或应用程序基础设施。由于恶意内容可能类似于普通的营销、编辑或信息材料，传统的提示注入和以恶意软件为重点的检测可能无法识别该活动。

description.en: Adversaries may attempt to use bots to successfully solve CAPTCHA challenges. CAPTCHA challenges are typically used by defenders to detect and prevent bot and spam traffic from accessing protected webpages. CAPTCHAs are automated tests often placed before login screens or form fields. Traditional CAPTCHAs ask the user to decipher a string of characters, type the characters into a box, and submit the form. reCAPTCHA asks the user to identify images, click a checkbox, or evaluate the user’s behavior from mouse movement and device cookies. Adversaries may use scripts or toolkits to automatically solve the CAPTCHA puzzle. For example, adversaries may develop a script that uses the ImageMagick toolkit to solve the CAPTCHA puzzles to then create multiple valid accounts. ImageMagick tool can convert the images into a RGB complemented image. The CAPTCHA challenge may be solved by identifying and comparing attributes of the RGB images to select the expected image. Once the CAPTCHA challenge is solved, the adversary’s script may access the protected page. After accessing the protected the page, the adversary may submit valid forms to the target.
description.zh: 对手可能试图使用机器人成功解决 CAPTCHA 挑战。防御者通常使用 CAPTCHA 挑战来检测和防止机器人和垃圾邮件流量访问受保护的网页。CAPTCHA 是通常放置在登录屏幕或表单字段之前的自动化测试。传统的 CAPTCHA 要求用户辨认一串字符，在框中输入字符并提交表单。reCAPTCHA 要求用户识别图像、单击复选框，或根据鼠标移动和设备 cookie 评估用户的行为。对手可能使用脚本或工具包自动解决 CAPTCHA 难题。例如，对手可能开发一个使用 ImageMagick 工具包解决 CAPTCHA 难题的脚本，然后创建多个有效账户。ImageMagick 工具可以将图像转换为 RGB 补色图像。CAPTCHA 挑战可以通过识别和比较 RGB 图像的属性来选择预期图像来解决。一旦 CAPTCHA 挑战被解决，对手的脚本就可以访问受保护的页面。访问受保护的页面后，对手可以向目标提交有效表单。

detectionStrategies.name: Detection of Automated CAPTCHA

analytics.name: Analytic 2104
analytics.description: Successful CAPTCHA completion does not expose whether the challenge was solved manually, through automated tooling, through an AI-enabled solver, or through a third-party human-solving service. Providers may independently classify associated sessions as automated or bot-like, but this identifies suspicious automation rather than the method used to complete the CAPTCHA.

description.en: Adversaries may avoid CAPTCHA challenges by mimicking human behavior. Automation tests, such as CAPTCHA, are typically used by defenders to detect and prevent bot and spam traffic from accessing protected webpages. CAPTCHAs are often placed before login screens or form fields. Traditional CAPTCHAs ask the user to decipher a string of characters, type the characters into a box, and submit the form. reCAPTCHA asks the user to identify images, click a checkbox, or evaluate the user’s behavior from mouse movement and device cookies. Adversaries may attempt to avoid CAPTCHA challenges by constructing a bot that mimics human behavior through browser automation. The automated browser may mimic a human by Masquerading a Browser Fingerprint and through attributes such as session history, IP reputation, and the use of browser APIs. For example, adversaries may use Selenium browsers to simulate a human user. In the Selenium browsers, JavaScript is injected into the website’s Document Object Model (DOM). The injected script may modify browser attributes such as Audio Context and Voice engines, graphic rendering, installed fonts, and browser navigator objects.
description.zh: 对手可能通过模仿人类行为来规避 CAPTCHA 挑战。自动化测试（例如 CAPTCHA）通常被防御者用来检测和防止机器人和垃圾邮件流量访问受保护的网页。CAPTCHA 通常放置在登录屏幕或表单字段之前。传统的 CAPTCHA 要求用户辨认一串字符，在框中输入字符并提交表单。reCAPTCHA 要求用户识别图像、单击复选框，或根据鼠标移动和设备 cookie 评估用户的行为。对手可能试图通过构建一个通过浏览器自动化模仿人类行为的机器人来规避 CAPTCHA 挑战。自动化浏览器可能通过伪装浏览器指纹（Masquerading a Browser Fingerprint）以及会话历史、IP 信誉和浏览器 API 的使用等属性来模仿人类。例如，对手可能使用 Selenium 浏览器来模拟人类用户。在 Selenium 浏览器中，JavaScript 被注入到网站的文档对象模型（DOM）中。注入的脚本可以修改浏览器属性，例如 Audio Context 和语音引擎、图形渲染、已安装的字体和浏览器 navigator 对象。

description.en: Adversaries may use methods like Indirect Prompt Injection to disrupt, disable, or otherwise impair autonomous defensive capabilities such as LLM-assisted processing of malware, artifacts, or activity. This behavior may cause a system to ignore data, fail to alert on malicious activity, abort analysis, or to be disabled completely. Adversaries may include content in malware implants that mimic an LLM prompt scaffold that contains fake system messages in order to convince the LLM that it has encountered an error. Depending on the type of error, the LLM may abort analysis, truncate, or refuse to continue. Adversaries may also embed prompts in malware intended to stop agents or systems from analyzing the malware.
description.zh: 对手可能使用间接提示注入（Indirect Prompt Injection）等方法来中断、禁用或以其他方式削弱自主防御能力，例如 LLM 辅助的恶意软件、工件或活动处理。此行为可能导致系统忽略数据、无法对恶意活动发出警报、中止分析或被完全禁用。对手可能在恶意软件植入物中包含模仿 LLM 提示脚手架的内容，其中包含虚假的系统消息，以便让 LLM 相信它遇到了错误。根据错误类型，LLM 可能中止分析、截断或拒绝继续。对手还可能在恶意软件中嵌入旨在阻止代理或系统分析该恶意软件的提示。

description.en: Adversaries may utilize Direct Prompt Injection, Indirect Prompt Injection or other methods to instruct enterprise AI agents to exfiltrate data. When enterprise systems incorporate the use of AI assistants or other AI agents, adversaries may abuse these systems to weaponize sanctioned tools available to the agent. As an AI agent processes queries or ingests data, an injected prompt can cause the agent to use its tool connections in unauthorized or unintended ways. When AI agents are induced to exfiltrate data, other exfiltration techniques likely apply as well to transfer the information out of the network, such as Exfiltration to Code Repository or Exfiltration Over Web Service.
description.zh: 对手可能利用直接提示词注入（Direct Prompt Injection）、间接提示词注入（Indirect Prompt Injection）或其他方法，指示企业 AI 智能体外泄数据。当企业系统引入 AI 助手或其他 AI 智能体时，对手可能滥用这些系统，将智能体可用的合规工具武器化。当 AI 智能体处理查询或摄取数据时，注入的提示词可能导致智能体以未授权或非预期的方式使用其工具连接。当 AI 智能体被诱导外泄数据时，很可能还会结合其他外泄技术将信息传出网络，例如外泄到代码仓库（Exfiltration to Code Repository）或通过 Web 服务外泄（Exfiltration Over Web Service）。
